A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASCL/IFPO study and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E. Reformatting does not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot, post-training, reasoning-benchmark and ablation results for Qwen3 models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, with several revised numerical entries.

M1.justification: The adaptive safety-rule retrieval procedure, behavior-cloning pipeline, reward components and IFPO advantage reweighting remain unchanged, including the implementation procedure in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Salad-Bench and OR-Bench training coverage and the same safety, over-refusal and general-reasoning evaluation datasets. Appendix D retains all dataset entries.

E2.justification: The prompt/RAG, SafeChain, STAR-1, STAR-1-mix, BC, GRPO and surrogate comparisons are retained. Tables 1–2 rename Agent to ASCL-ZS, matching the existing zero-shot method.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, dataset sizes, sampling settings, judges and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–D. Figure 4 corrects a safety-axis label without changing the underlying metric or evaluation design.

E4.justification: The surrogate-CoT, rule-penalty and GRPO/IFPO ablations, consultation-rate analyses and qualitative example are retained. No analysis is added, removed or redesigned; Figure 4 has localized numerical corrections.

E5.justification: Both versions report 16 evaluations for MATH-500, eight for GSM8K and single evaluations for the other benchmarks, and retain the fixed RL data-shuffling seed statement. No uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is added.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises all five 8B IFPO over-refusal entries, making them consistent with the retained 4.33 average. Table 2 changes 8B STAR-1 MATH-500 from 84.17 to 96.28, its reasoning average from 78.66 to 81.08 and H-avg. from 83.30 to 84.19. Figure 4 changes 4B IFPO compliance from 93.16 to 94.00 and H-avg. from 89.56 to 89.82. These are localized revisions under unchanged reported settings.

T1.justification: The reward equation, IFPO definitions and weighting equations, and Appendix E harmonic-mean definition are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that adaptive rule retrieval and IFPO improve the safety–utility trade-off and that direct rule memorization is insufficient. The added closing aspiration does not expand the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations involving rigid refusal patterns, excessive rule consultation and distribution mismatch. Section 5.3 continues to state that safety-related reasoning does not demonstrate generalization to general reasoning capabilities.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code availability statement and project repository link in the abstract; v1 has no project-code link. The documented training settings, hardware information, prompts and implementation procedures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds references on open-ended and test-time reasoning, including Tan, Wang and Yu (2026). The Yan et al. reference changes from Stop Tracking Me! to What if Consensus Lies?. The central safety-alignment positioning and Section 2 discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain intact. v2 makes limited introduction and conclusion edits, adds acknowledgements, standardizes Agent to ASCL-ZS in tables, and updates author and bibliographic presentation.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into an ICML layout, changing the title/affiliation block, running headers, typography, column dimensions, figure/table placement and appendix prompt wrapping. All eight figures and four tables remain. Figure 4 corrects Attack Success Rate to Defense Success Rate; Figure 8 introduces malformed comparison/filter symbols in the displayed template.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves concrete reporting inconsistencies: Table 1's 8B IFPO entries now match its average, and Figure 4's 4B values agree with the tables while its safety axis is correctly labeled. Consistent method names and an explicit project-code link also improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. Figure 8's malformed operators are a localized regression, but the empirical-reporting repairs support a modest net improvement.
